The `blowhorn config` commands. Each one's `--help` prints the same text.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [`config get`](#blowhorn-config-get) | Print one option's effective value, which layer supplied it (a flag, the environment, the file or the built-in) and which document holds it. |
| [`config path`](#blowhorn-config-path) | Print the effective global config file path. |
| [`config set`](#blowhorn-config-set) | Set a dotted key in the global config file, keeping the file's comments, key order and unknown keys as written. |
| [`config show`](#blowhorn-config-show) | Display the current global config file contents, followed by the private connection file that defaults.store.config points at (~/.config/blowhorn/store.yaml, mode 0600) with store.password reported... |

## blowhorn config get

Print one option's effective value, which layer supplied it (a flag, the environment, the file or the built-in) and which document holds it: .blowhorn.yaml for defaults.&lt;name&gt;, the private connection file for store.&lt;name&gt;. store.password is reported as set or not set and never printed. With --json, the same row 'config show --json' carries for the option.

```text
blowhorn config get [OPTIONS] key
```

| Argument | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | yes | Dotted option key: defaults.&lt;name&gt; lives in .blowhorn.yaml, store.&lt;name&gt; in the private connection file |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--json` | boolean | `false` | Emit the option report as machine-readable JSON |
| `--platform` | string |  | Accepted and ignored by 'blowhorn config': this command never acts on a platform, so --platform has no effect here -- including a value inherited from BLOWHORN_PLATFORM or defaults.platform in .blowhorn.yaml |
| `--pace` | string |  | Accepted by 'blowhorn config get' because --pace is a global flag, but this command does no paced work -- it sleeps between nothing -- so the value changes nothing about how it runs and appears only in the Pace column of the -v summary. Resolved as CLI flag, then BLOWHORN_PACE, then defaults.pace in .blowhorn.yaml (normal when none is set); an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs |

Also takes the [shared flags](/docs/reference/cli/shared-flags/): `--config`, `--log-dir`, `--profile`, `--exclude`, `--headless`, `--chrome-launch`, `--headed`, `--dry-run`, `--verbose`.

Examples:

```bash
blowhorn config get defaults.profile
blowhorn config get store.password
blowhorn config get store.tunnel.remote --json
```

Output: json with --json, text otherwise.

## blowhorn config set

Set a dotted key in the global config file, keeping the file's comments, key order and unknown keys as written. A key the engine reads is stored in its own type (defaults.headless becomes a boolean, defaults.exclude a list even for one name, an empty value clears the key); for any other key, true/false become booleans and comma-delimited values become lists. A store.&lt;name&gt; key -- the database connection and the bastion tunnel -- is written to the private connection file that defaults.store.config points at (~/.config/blowhorn/store.yaml, created at mode 0600 in a 0700 directory) and never to .blowhorn.yaml, which git tracks. 'store.password' with no value prompts for it, so the password is never in argv or the daily log; an empty read -- no stdin, or a blank line -- is refused and nothing is written, so the one way to clear a stored password is the explicit empty argument "blowhorn config set store.password ''". A value that starts with a dash is read as an option unless you end the options first: write "blowhorn config set &lt;key&gt; -- &lt;value&gt;", which is also how a refused value gets the sentence saying what a valid one is.

```text
blowhorn config set [OPTIONS] key [value]
```

| Argument | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | yes | Dotted option key: defaults.&lt;name&gt; lives in .blowhorn.yaml, store.&lt;name&gt; in the private connection file |
| `value` | no | Value to assign to the key. Leave it out for store.password to be prompted for it instead; an empty prompt clears nothing, so pass an explicit '' to clear a stored value |

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--json` | boolean | `false` | Emit the option report as machine-readable JSON |
| `--platform` | string |  | Accepted and ignored by 'blowhorn config': this command never acts on a platform, so --platform has no effect here -- including a value inherited from BLOWHORN_PLATFORM or defaults.platform in .blowhorn.yaml |
| `--pace` | string |  | Accepted by 'blowhorn config set' because --pace is a global flag, but this command does no paced work -- it sleeps between nothing -- so the value changes nothing about how it runs and appears only in the Pace column of the -v summary. Resolved as CLI flag, then BLOWHORN_PACE, then defaults.pace in .blowhorn.yaml (normal when none is set); an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs |

Also takes the [shared flags](/docs/reference/cli/shared-flags/): `--config`, `--log-dir`, `--profile`, `--exclude`, `--headless`, `--chrome-launch`, `--headed`, `--dry-run`, `--verbose`.

Examples:

```bash
blowhorn config set defaults.profile lee
blowhorn config set defaults.pace slow
blowhorn config set defaults.exclude layer5,lee,meshery,kanvas
blowhorn config set defaults.logs.directory ~/blowhorn-logs
blowhorn config set defaults.logs.retention_days 365
blowhorn config set defaults.logs.retention_days -- -1
blowhorn config set defaults.exclude ''
blowhorn config set defaults.headless true --json
blowhorn config set defaults.store.organization layer5
blowhorn config set store.tunnel.target someone@bastion.example.com
blowhorn config set store.password
blowhorn config set store.password ''
```

Output: json with --json, text otherwise.

## blowhorn config show

Display the current global config file contents, followed by the private connection file that defaults.store.config points at (~/.config/blowhorn/store.yaml, mode 0600) with store.password reported as set or not set and never printed. With --json, report every option .blowhorn.yaml honours instead: the value stored in the file, the environment override in force, the effective value and which of them supplied it, plus any keys under defaults the engine does not read; the private file's options are read with 'blowhorn config get' and 'blowhorn store --json'.

```text
blowhorn config show [OPTIONS]
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--json` | boolean | `false` | Emit the option report as machine-readable JSON |
| `--platform` | string |  | Accepted and ignored by 'blowhorn config': this command never acts on a platform, so --platform has no effect here -- including a value inherited from BLOWHORN_PLATFORM or defaults.platform in .blowhorn.yaml |
| `--pace` | string |  | Accepted by 'blowhorn config show' because --pace is a global flag, but this command does no paced work -- it sleeps between nothing -- so the value changes nothing about how it runs and appears only in the Pace column of the -v summary. Resolved as CLI flag, then BLOWHORN_PACE, then defaults.pace in .blowhorn.yaml (normal when none is set); an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs |

Also takes the [shared flags](/docs/reference/cli/shared-flags/): `--config`, `--log-dir`, `--profile`, `--exclude`, `--headless`, `--chrome-launch`, `--headed`, `--dry-run`, `--verbose`.

Examples:

```bash
blowhorn config show
blowhorn config show --config ~/.blowhorn.yaml
blowhorn config show --json
```

Output: json with --json, text otherwise.
